name: jimoholayinka01/Revolut-Spending
what_it_holds: End-to-end time series analysis/forecasting project on Revolut debit-card spending data in the UK, examining transaction trends by age demographic and seasonality. Not confirmed whether the underlying dataset is real Revolut transaction data, a public Revolut aggregate release, or a synthetic/Kaggle stand-in — needs a directory-listing check before relying on it.
why_useful: If the underlying data is genuine (even anonymized/aggregated) UK fintech card-spend data with seasonality, it is a private-sector analogue to ONS card spending (gap #6) for UK consumer strength, which reads on EMEA nights/ADR. Unverified provenance keeps this at medium-low until checked.
themes: Public consumer-spend panels: Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker (Affinity card spend), ONS card spending, Bank of England CHAPS, BBVA/CaixaBank research open data, Banco de Portugal SIBS, Norges Bank card data
why_all: If the underlying data is genuine (even anonymized/aggregated) UK fintech card-spend data with seasonality, it is a private-sector analogue to ONS card spending (gap #6) for UK consumer strength, which reads on EMEA nights/ADR. Unverified provenance keeps this at medium-low until checked.

name: bbk
what_it_holds: R client package for German/European central bank APIs; `bbk_data()` pulls arbitrary Bundesbank statistics-API series by flow ID + data key (example shown is a daily yield curve). Pure API wrapper, no committed data files, but actively maintained (updated 12 Sep 2026).
why_useful: One-command programmatic access to any Bundesbank series, including (if the flow ID is supplied) the Bundesbank weekly activity index named in this theme, plus other German high-frequency series (retail, trade, FX) relevant to EMEA consumer strength regional splits.
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
why_all: One-command programmatic access to any Bundesbank series, including (if the flow ID is supplied) the Bundesbank weekly activity index named in this theme, plus other German high-frequency series (retail, trade, FX) relevant to EMEA consumer strength regional splits.

name: fredr
what_it_holds: R bindings to the FRED API; example calls return realtime_start/realtime_end columns confirming ALFRED vintage support. 101 stars, 242 commits, MIT-style license, active (recent examples dated 2021+, CI enabled).
why_useful: Another mature, well-maintained R client covering the same point-in-time macro-vintage need as fredapi/alfred (gap #4); wider adoption (101 stars) than onnokleen/alfred so likely more battle-tested for edge cases.
duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with onnokleen/alfred and fredapi in function
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Another mature, well-maintained R client covering the same point-in-time macro-vintage need as fredapi/alfred (gap #4); wider adoption (101 stars) than onnokleen/alfred so likely more battle-tested for edge cases.

name: fedfred
what_it_holds: Feature-rich Python package covering FRED, GeoFRED, ALFRED, and FRASER APIs; native Pandas/Polars/Dask support, async requests, local caching, rate limiting. MIT licensed, 359 commits, v3.0.0, 9 stars.
why_useful: Newer/broader alternative to fredapi with explicit ALFRED support plus GeoFRED (regional/state series, useful for the STR-regulation and regional-macro gaps) and caching for repeated point-in-time backtests.
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Newer/broader alternative to fredapi with explicit ALFRED support plus GeoFRED (regional/state series, useful for the STR-regulation and regional-macro gaps) and caching for repeated point-in-time backtests.

name: peruvian_gdp_revisions (Peru Real-Time GDP dataset pipeline)
what_it_holds: Python pipeline (scrape -> OCR for pre-2013 scans -> clean -> vintage-format / releases-format output) that reconstructs a real-time GDP vintage dataset for Peru from BCRP Weekly Reports, 1994-2025 (monthly and quarterly/annual). Actual processed vintage CSV/Parquet outputs are hosted on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18099975); GitHub repo (MIT, 1,289 commits, 1 star) holds only the code. Includes OCR for scanned pre-2013 PDFs.
why_useful: A genuine, working real-time/vintage GDP dataset construction for a LatAm economy (gap #7 regional travel/macro outside US/EU is adjacent; more directly this is a template + actual vintage dataset for point-in-time macro data outside the US ALFRED system, filling the 'ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages... elsewhere' spirit of this theme for a market ABNB reports LatAm revenue in).
size_hint: dataset hosted externally on Zenodo; pipeline code in repo
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: A genuine, working real-time/vintage GDP dataset construction for a LatAm economy (gap #7 regional travel/macro outside US/EU is adjacent; more directly this is a template + actual vintage dataset for point-in-time macro data outside the US ALFRED system, filling the 'ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages... elsewhere' spirit of this theme for a market ABNB reports LatAm revenue in).
